summary: Join our comprehensive training on Emerging Markets and Financial Development to gain insights into financial systems and investment opportunities worldwide.
lede: Environmental law in real estate affects land use, development, transactions, leasing, and property operations. For developers, property and asset managers, acquisition teams, and facilities professionals, the course addresses how to identify environmental risks and liabilities, interpret environmental assessment findings, and include environmental responsibilities in due diligence, contracts, and compliance processes. It also covers planning approvals, pollution, climate risks, and community engagement.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who interact with real estate assets and must understand environmental laws and regulatory risk. This course is designed for: Real estate developers and project sponsors. Property and asset managers responsible for ongoing compliance. Corporate real estate managers overseeing office, industrial, or retail portfolios. Land acquisition, due diligence, and investment teams. Facilities and operations managers in large commercial or industrial sites. Public sector staff involved in planning approvals and enforcement. Environmental and social safeguard officers in development finance institutions. Legal, risk, and compliance professionals who support real estate transactions. Construction, engineering, and infrastructure project managers. NGO or civil society professionals engaging with real estate, land use, and community impacts.
modules: Foundations of Environmental Law in Real Estate
Land Use, Zoning, and Planning Approvals
Environmental Due Diligence in Transactions and Leasing
Climate Risk, Resilience, and Real Estate Regulation
Green Building Standards and ESG in Property
Community, Stakeholder Engagement, and Social Safeguards
Enforcement, Disputes, and Legal Risk Management
Building an Environmental Compliance Culture in Real Estate
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of real estate development processes and a willingness to engage in scenario-based learning. Prior experience in property management or development is beneficial but not required.
